newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD official slams Waigel's gold plan.
newsitem.headline: German SPD official slams Waigel's gold plan.

text.p: A key official in the German opposition Social Democrat party on Wednesday lashed out at government plans to revalue the German central bank's gold and foreign exchange reserves to drum up a special profit.

Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier, the opposition SPD's financial expert, told German radio that she rejected the idea of a revaluation of the gold reserves at the current time combined with an early transfer of special profit to the government.
"Operation gold hoard clearly damages the reputation of the Bundesbank and of European monetary union," she said.
She added that the impression was correct that "this tweaking of balance sheets is being done to reach the criteria for the euro."

Although few details of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan have been released, it appears that his scheme calls on the Bundesbank to transfer an unrealised profit to Bonn's coffers to help ease the tight position of public finances.
The German central bank is debating the issue at a council meeting today.
Matthaeus-Maier said that she had no opposition to the actual idea of revaluing the reserves, adding that other countries such as the Netherlands had taken similar steps.
"But nobody there came up with this mad idea that the process could be used to transfer a higher, premature profit to the government," she said.

The Dutch central bank regularly reviews the value at which its reserves are held in the balance sheet. But it does not pay out an unrealised profit as a result. Instead the reserve values are balanced out in the asset and liability account.
Matthaeus-Maier noted that Waigel's plans had already caused a storm of comment and protest.
"That must be ended immediately and not strengthened by this senseless hectic activity aimed at pushing through a change in the (Bundesbank) law before the summer break," she said.
